# Psalm 9 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choirmaster. According to Muth-labben. A psalm of David.

**2** I will give thanks to the LORD with my whole heart; I will recount all Your wonderful deeds.

**3** I will be glad and exult in You; I will sing praise to Your name, O Most High.

**4** When my enemies turn back, they stumble and perish before You.

**5** For You have maintained my just cause; You have sat on the throne, judging righteously.

**6** You have rebuked the nations; You have destroyed the wicked. You have blotted out their name forever and ever.

**7** The enemy — desolations have come to a perpetual end; You have uprooted their cities — the very memory of them has perished.

**8** But the LORD sits enthroned forever; He has established His throne for judgment.

**9** He judges the world in righteousness; He renders judgment to the peoples with equity.

**10** The LORD is a stronghold for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble.

**11** Those who know Your name put their trust in You, for You, O LORD, have not forsaken those who seek You.

**12** Sing praises to the LORD, who dwells in Zion! Declare among the peoples His deeds!

**13** For He who avenges blood is mindful of them; He does not forget the cry of the afflicted.

**14** Be gracious to me, O LORD! See my affliction from those who hate me, O You who lift me up from the gates of death,

**15** that I may recount all Your praises, that in the gates of the daughter of Zion I may rejoice in Your salvation.

**16** The nations have sunk in the pit that they made; in the net that they hid, their own foot has been caught.

**17** The LORD has made Himself known; He has executed judgment. The wicked is snared in the work of his own hands. Higgaion. Selah.

**18** The wicked shall return to Sheol — all the nations that forget God.

**19** For the needy shall not always be forgotten, and the hope of the afflicted shall not perish forever.

**20** Arise, O LORD! Let not man prevail; let the nations be judged before You.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 9.

- **9:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **9:4** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **9:9** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **9:12** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **9:15** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **9:16** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **9:1**: Muth-labben — possibly 'death of the son,' a tune name. The meaning is debated.
- **9:17**: Higgaion — a musical term, possibly meaning 'meditation' or a soft, murmured musical interlude.

### LOGOS
- **9:8-9**: The dual image of God's throne: it is both eternal (v.8) and active in justice (v.9). God reigns and judges simultaneously.
- **9:10**: 'Those who know Your name' — knowing God's name means knowing His character. Trust is grounded in experience, not theory.

### PNEUMA
- **9:16-17**: Poetic justice is a recurring theme in the Psalms: the wicked fall into their own traps. Justice is not imposed from outside — it grows from the nature of evil itself.
- **9:18-19**: The psalm refuses to let poverty be permanent. God's justice includes economic reversal — the forgotten will be remembered.

— SOPHIA
